cards.subject: Physics
cards.back: F = ma — Force equals mass times acceleration. The acceleration of a body is directly proportional to the force applied and inversely proportional to its mass.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.back: Final velocity = initial velocity + acceleration × time. Used when acceleration is constant.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.back: Distance = (initial velocity × time) + ½ × acceleration × time². This is the second equation of motion.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.back: v² = u² + 2as. Third equation of motion relating velocities, acceleration, and distance. Doesn't require time.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.back: n = c/v = 1/sin C = sin i / sin r. Where c = speed of light in vacuum, v = speed in medium, C = critical angle, i = angle of incidence, r = angle of refraction.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.back: v = fλ — Wave speed equals frequency × wavelength. Units: v (m/s), f (Hz), λ (m).

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.back: PV = nRT — Pressure × Volume = moles × gas constant × temperature. R = 8.31 J/(mol·K) or 0.082 L·atm/(mol·K).

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.back: pH = -log[H⁺] — pH measures acidity. pH < 7 is acidic, pH = 7 is neutral, pH > 7 is alkaline (basic).

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.back: n = m/M — Number of moles = mass (g) / molar mass (g/mol). Also n = N/Nₐ where N = number of particles, Nₐ = 6.02 × 10²³.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.back: 1 mole of any gas at STP occupies 22.4 litres. STP = Standard Temperature and Pressure (0°C, 1 atm).

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.back: C = n/V — Concentration (mol/L) = moles of solute / volume of solution (L). Also expressed as c(mol/dm³).

cards.subject: Biology
cards.back: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O →(light, chlorophyll)→ C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂. Raw materials: CO₂ and water. Products: glucose and oxygen. Occurs in chloroplasts.

cards.subject: Biology
cards.back: C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + energy (ATP). Occurs in mitochondria. Produces about 38 ATP molecules per glucose.

cards.subject: Biology
cards.back: Cell wall, cell membrane, nucleus, cytoplasm, chloroplasts, vacuole (large central), mitochondria, ribosomes, endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus.

cards.subject: Biology
cards.back: 1) Detoxification of poisons, 2) Production of bile, 3) Storage of glycogen, 4) Breakdown of red blood cells, 5) Metabolism of proteins and fats.

cards.subject: Biology
cards.back: Cell → Tissue → Organ → Organ System → Organism → Population → Community → Ecosystem → Biome.

cards.subject: Mathematics
cards.back: b^y = x. The logarithm tells you what power the base must be raised to, to get x. Example: log₂(8) = 3 because 2³ = 8.

cards.subject: Mathematics
cards.back: x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac)) / 2a. For ax² + bx + c = 0. The discriminant b² - 4ac determines the nature of roots.

cards.subject: Mathematics
cards.back: Sₙ = n/2 × [2a + (n-1)d] or Sₙ = n/2 × (a + l), where a = first term, d = common difference, l = last term, n = number of terms.

cards.subject: Mathematics
cards.back: sin θ = Opposite/Hypotenuse, cos θ = Adjacent/Hypotenuse, tan θ = Opposite/Adjacent. Remember: SOH-CAH-TOA.

cards.subject: Mathematics
cards.back: d/dx(xⁿ) = nxⁿ⁻¹. The derivative of x raised to power n is n times x raised to power (n-1).

cards.subject: Further Maths
cards.back: a·b = |a||b|cos θ. If a = (x₁,y₁) and b = (x₂,y₂), then a·b = x₁x₂ + y₁y₂. The result is a scalar.

cards.subject: Further Maths
cards.back: For A = [a b; c d], det(A) = ad - bc. If det = 0, the matrix has no inverse (singular matrix).

cards.subject: Further Maths
cards.back: Impulse = Force × time = Change in momentum = mv - mu. Units: Ns or kg·m/s.

cards.subject: Computer Science
cards.back: Multiply each bit by its place value (powers of 2) and add. E.g., 1011 = 1×8 + 0×4 + 1×2 + 1×1 = 11.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.back: V = IR — Voltage equals current × resistance. V (volts), I (amperes), R (ohms).

cards.subject: Physics
cards.back: F = ke — The restoring force of a spring is directly proportional to its extension, within the elastic limit. k = spring constant (N/m).

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.back: Rate₁/Rate₂ = √(M₂/M₁). The rate of diffusion of a gas is inversely proportional to the square root of its molar mass.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: General formula of alkanes, alkenes, alkynes
cards.back: Alkanes: CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ (saturated), Alkenes: CₙH₂ₙ (unsaturated, C=C), Alkynes: CₙH₂ₙ₋₂ (unsaturated, C≡C).

cards.subject: Biology
cards.back: The heart pumps blood through the body. Right side: deoxygenated blood to lungs. Left side: oxygenated blood to body. Beats ~72 times per minute.
